question: Bitot's spots — triangular, foamy, greyish-white deposits on the bulbar conjunctiva — are a specific clinical sign of Vitamin A deficiency.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Bitot's spots are the hallmark clinical sign of Vitamin A deficiency. The National Vitamin A Supplementation Programme provides megadose Vitamin A (1,00,000 IU at 9 months; 2,00,000 IU every 6 months from 18 months to 5 years) to prevent this.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Bitot's spots (WHO classification XB) are pathognomonic for Vitamin A deficiency. They represent squamous metaplasia and keratinisation of the conjunctiva and should prompt immediate Vitamin A supplementation.
